reason:
The measurements check out exactly - I reproduced panel 597..1156, Done 1036, Delete 1100, scrollY 0, .b-edit position:relative and keepInBand's early return at 1440x960, 1280x900, 1152x800, 1024x768 and 1279x800 - and the gate genuinely never looks (interaction-check.mjs:978 runs its band loop only at 390 and 768, and every desk-width click on [data-act=done]/[data-act=delete] goes through Playwright's own auto-scroll, so off-screen is invisible to it). The finding is refuted on its fix, which I drove both halves of and which makes the surface worse, not better.

Half (1) alone - the static branch in keepInBand - is a runaway scroll pump. keepInBand is called after EVERY setAway via the rAF at render-b.js:645 and again from land(). With .b-stick still sticky the panel is pinned at 406..965 no matter where the document sits, so scrollBy can never satisfy box.bottom <= innerHeight and never converges. Measured, calling it repeatedly with the CSS half absent: 1024x768 scrolls 404, then 213, then 213, then 213 with the panel's viewport rect unchanged at 406..965 the whole time; 1152x800 pumps 372 then 181 forever. That is the round-7 objection in its purest form - the plan slides out from under a stationary editor, one 213px lurch per stepper press, walking the owner to the foot of the document while the steppers hold still under the hand.

Half (2) - [data-editor-open] .b-stick{position:static} - stops the pump but buys it by breaking the head instead of the foot. Driven at every desk width, opening the editor on the first row actually visible at that scroll position: at scrollY 0 the fix works (1024x768 scrolls 404, panel 193..752, Done 632, Delete 696, row at 166 - all on screen). But from scrollY 600 the sticky release yanks the whole horizon column up 409px the instant the panel appears, and from 900 it yanks it 709px: panel lands at -3..556 and -303..256, and the proposed scrollBy returns 0 because it only ever corrects box.bottom, never box.top. So the panel's first 3px and then 303px are above the fold - which is the reserved 88px band and, at 900, the WHEN field with it. The reversibility bar lives at top:16 inside that reserve (b.css:854), so at scrollY 900 the undo bar sits at -287: a move made there reports itself into a control the owner cannot see or press. Round 7 already refuted moving that band on exactly this ground ('it puts the undo bar off screen'). And at 1440x960 this is a straight regression - unfixed, opening from scrollY 300/600/900 puts BOTH Done and Delete on screen (845 and 909 against 960); with the fix the panel head goes off screen instead. Round 7's objection is not evaded, only relocated.

Two further couplings the fix does not account for: releasing the pin silently kills the gap-note writer, which early-returns unless getComputedStyle(stick).position === 'sticky' (render-b.js:1103), so the horizon sentence freezes at 'Nothing is planned until 1 August' for the whole edit - the stale-sentence defect that comment records as already paid for; and the same static branch now fires inside land(), which round 7 hardened specifically so undo returns the owner to where they were standing.

What is left standing is a real problem, and it is bigger than 'on open': at 1152x800 and 1024x768 the pinned panel puts Done at 845 and Delete at 909 off screen at EVERY scroll position I tested (0, 300, 600, 900), reachable only at the document's absolute end. But that is the overlapping claim another seat raised, and it is not curable by either edit proposed here. The rail cannot hold a 366px horizon plus a 559px editor in a 768px viewport, so the answer is to make the sticky box itself fit - cap .b-stick's height when the editor is open and let the rail scroll internally, or shorten the panel at desk width - not to unpin the column and push the page around under the owner's hand.
